About CTP

CTP is Europe’s largest listed developer, owner, and operator of logistics and industrial real estate by gross leasable area ("GLA"), with a portfolio of 15.1 million sqm of GLA in 12 countries and 1.7 million sqm under construction as of 30 September 2026. The company’s ready-built factories and warehouses, together with its custom-built solutions, serve over 1,700 clients ranging from large blue-chip multinationals to local SMEs. CTP builds long-term partnerships through a client-first approach, maintaining roughly 93% annual retention and generating 63% of new business from existing client expansion. All new buildings are certified to the BREEAM standard "Very Good" or higher, underscoring the company’s commitment to sustainable development. CTP holds Investment Grade ratings from S&P: BBB (Negative), Moody’s: Baa2 (Stable), and JCR: A (Stable).

For more information, visit www.ctp.eu.

data.title: Maybank Profit Climbs on Stronger Fee Income, Beating Estimates — Update
data.description:
By Ying Xian Wong

Malayan Banking posted stronger-than-expected net profit in the third quarter, driven by higher core fee income and net fund-based income.

Malaysia's largest lender by market capitalization said Monday that quarterly net profit rose 4.7% from a year earlier to 2.74 billion ringgit, equivalent to $666.2 million. Analysts polled by Visible Alpha had expected 2.71 billion ringgit.

A 7.7% increase in core fees, led by higher wealth-management and investment banking-related income, supported the bottom line, Maybank said. Net fund-based income also grew, rising 2.3% to 5.12 billion ringgit as net interest margin improved five basis points to 2.07%.

However, net interest income--the difference between interest earned on loans and that paid on deposits--slipped 4.3% to 3.13 billion ringgit, and noninterest income fell 3.2% to 2.38 billion ringgit, it said.

Net impairment provisions for the quarter declined 39% to 215.2 million ringgit.

Maybank Chief Executive Khairussaleh Ramli said that while its diversified businesses and regional operations supported performance, the group remains cautious about the outlook amid global economic challenges and geopolitical uncertainty.

Shares of the Malaysian lender have declined nearly 5% this year, pressured by concerns about funding costs and net interest margins as bond yields rise amid a more hawkish Federal Reserve outlook.

The planned expansion of the Kuala Lumpur Composite Index to 50 constituents from 30, aimed at reducing the index's concentration in financial stocks, has also weighed on sentiment toward the bank, an index heavyweight.

Analysts said a potential rate hike by Malaysia's central bank next March could offer Malaysian banks some respite. Banks' net interest margins have been squeezed as U.S. Treasury yields lift domestic bond yields and funding costs and intense deposit competition pushes lenders to offer higher rates.

A 25-basis-point increase in Bank Negara Malaysia's policy rate could improve Maybank's net interest margin by 2.6 basis points, according to estimates by CIMB Securities, which is overweight on the Malaysia banking sector.

That relief would likely be temporary, however. The potential rate increase is a short-term positive catalyst for banks' margins rather than a structural solution to the sector's funding challenges, CIMB Securities analyst Ei Leen Tan said.

data.title: Partners Group to Buy New Zealand Transport Firm From Morgan Stanley Infrastructure Partners
data.description:
By Fabiana Negrin Ochoa

Private-markets firm Partners Group has agreed to acquire a New Zealand transport firm from Morgan Stanley Infrastructure Partners amid rising client demand for income-oriented infrastructure assets.

Partners Group, which oversees more than $186 billion in assets, said it will invest in StraitNZ from select pools of capital and plans to work with management to further grow the company's recurring revenue base.

No financial terms were disclosed.

StraitNZ is an integrated transport, logistics and ferry company managing freight and passenger services across the Cook Strait. It is one of two ferry operators connecting New Zealand's national highway system from the North Island to the South Island.

Nicholas Kuys, managing director for infrastructure at Partners Group, said the company holds a defensive position on the transport route that's a backbone of the New Zealand economy.

Morgan Stanley Infrastructure Partners said that since it invested in the company in March 2022, StraitNZ has delivered strong growth in earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization.

The deal is in line with Partners Group's expectations that the trend of client demand for strategic brownfield investments will accelerate as more investors recognize the benefits of exposure to such assets.

The transaction is expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to customary regulatory approvals and other conditions.
